appended_meaning:
The materially referenced publicity/lobbying funding conditions are compared at complete section 503(a)-(c) in PL113-235 division G 2015, PL115-31 division H 2017, PL116-94 division A 2020 and PL117-328 division H 2023. Each subsection (a) and (b) covers an appropriation contained in its Act/division or funds transferred pursuant to PPACA section 4002. Both covered-money branches remain explicit; this is not every Federal dollar, every private contribution or every health-service payment. The established section 3 division-reference rule and literal dated health-transfer chain remain, without finding that a current grant receives either category of covered funds.

Complete 503(a) retains the normal and recognized executive-legislative relationships qualification. It restricts covered funds used for publicity or propaganda purposes and the preparation, distribution or use of the listed kit/pamphlet/booklet/publication/electronic/radio/television/video materials designed to support or defeat enactment of legislation before Congress or State/local legislative bodies, except in presentation to Congress or the State/local legislature itself. It separately covers materials designed to support or defeat proposed or pending regulation, administrative action or orders issued by the executive branch of State/local government, except in presentation to that executive branch itself. Legislative-body and State/local-executive presentation exceptions remain separate; the printed State/local-executive object is not expanded here into every Federal regulatory communication or a universal ban on ordinary information.

Complete 503(b) separately restricts use of covered funds to pay the salary or expenses of a grant or contract recipient, or an agent acting for that recipient, related to an activity designed to influence enactment of the named legislation, appropriations, regulation, administrative action or Executive order proposed or pending before Congress, State government, State legislature or local legislative bodies. Both the recipient/agent and salary/expenses nexus remain. Its qualifications preserve normal and recognized executive-legislative relationships and participation by an agency or officer of a State, local or tribal government in policymaking and administrative processes within that government's executive branch. The tribal-government process qualification is not dropped merely because the separate subsection (a) presentation objects say State/local. No actual communication, salary charge, recipient conduct or violation is found.

Complete 503(c) says the subsection (a)/(b) prohibitions include activities advocating or promoting proposed, pending or future Federal/State/local tax increases and proposed, pending or future requirements or restrictions on legal consumer products, including sale or marketing and including but not limited to advocacy or promotion of gun control. Future proposals, the legal-consumer-product object, sale/marketing context and nonexclusive gun-control example remain together. This is inclusion within the qualified covered-funding prohibitions, not only a gun-related clause, a ban on every person's policy discussion, a finding of improper advocacy or a separate immigration/gun/tax/lobbying position attributed to a member from the package vote.

The named section 4002 authority establishes the Prevention and Public Health Fund, administered through HHS's Office of the Secretary for expanded and sustained national investment in prevention and public-health programs. Its subsection (c) directs the Secretary to transfer Fund amounts to HHS accounts to increase funding over the fiscal year 2008 level for programs authorized by the Public Health Service Act and the specified prevention, wellness and public-health activities. Its subsection (d) allows the House and Senate Appropriations Committees to provide for transfers to eligible activities, subject to subsection (c). The original same-Act 10401(b) substitutions add the research/health-screenings/initiatives wording and change the outreach-campaign wording to Regarding Preventive; they remain bound alongside original 4002 and the distinct 2024 Code identity at 42 USC 300u-11. The original and amended funding schedules are preserved as versioned source evidence, not declared identical or applied to every earlier period/current grant. This Fund is not silently substituted for the separate assessment-funded Domestic Trafficking Victims' Fund health-transfer source, the CHC account or every PHS program; no actual Fund transfer, program eligibility, new individual benefit or current grant amount is inferred.

The four complete 503 clauses match at the reviewed operative extent after private comparison removes original notes/page markers and normalizes only the known executive- legislative word-wrap spacing. Governed bytes, glyphs, annotations, line-wrap spelling, years and division identities remain unchanged. The comparison does not resolve all dated funding/carry-forward applications. This source-grounded member-neutral context remains part of the whole H.R. 1968 passage meaning; shared compacts, recorded choices, counting, eligibility, prior needle-program version differences and the compiled proposition graph remain unchanged.

This completes only selected publicity/lobbying conditions and the named Fund-transfer identity/pathways at the captured extents. Other material program/HHS/general conditions, all referenced PHS program application, historical funding-chain application, actual current grant coverage and remaining package authorities remain executable research. Unfinished research is not unavailable evidence. All 70 separate application questions, including frozen Q68/Q69/Q70, remain unchanged. No full conditions/fund/package/domain closure, independent acceptance, production eligibility or publication is declared.

operative_witnesses.passage:
SEC. 4002. PREVENTION <<NOTE: 42 USC 300u-11.>> AND PUBLIC HEALTH FUND. (a) Purpose.--It is the purpose of this section to establish a Prevention and Public Health Fund (referred to in this section as the ``Fund''), to be administered through the Department of Health and Human Services, Office of the Secretary, to provide for expanded and sustained national investment in prevention and public health programs to improve health and help restrain the rate of growth in private and public sector health care costs. (b) Funding.--There are hereby authorized to be appropriated, and appropriated, to the Fund, out of any monies in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated-- (1) for fiscal year 2010, $500,000,000; (2) for fiscal year 2011, $750,000,000; (3) for fiscal year 2012, $1,000,000,000; (4) for fiscal year 2013, $1,250,000,000; (5) for fiscal year 2014, $1,500,000,000; and (6) for fiscal year 2015, and each fiscal year thereafter, $2,000,000,000. (c) Use of Fund.--The Secretary shall transfer amounts in the Fund to accounts within the Department of Health and Human Services to increase funding, over the fiscal year 2008 level, for programs authorized by the Public Health Service Act, for prevention, wellness, and public health activities including prevention research and health screenings, such as the Community Transformation grant program, the Education and Outreach Campaign for Preventive Benefits, and immunization programs. (d) Transfer Authority.--The Committee on Appropriations of the Senate and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives may provide for the transfer of funds in the Fund to eligible activities under this section, subject to subsection (c). 

(b) Section 4002(c) of this Act <<NOTE: 42 USC 300u-11.>> is amended-- [[Page 124 STAT. 975]] (1) by striking ``research and health screenings'' and inserting ``research, health screenings, and initiatives''; and (2) by striking ``for Preventive'' and inserting ``Regarding Preventive''.
operative_witnesses.locator: Complete original PPACA section 4002(a)-(d) and same-Act section 10401(b) amendments to 4002(c): named Prevention and Public Health Fund identity/purpose, original funding schedule, HHS transfer for PHS-authorized prevention/public-health programs and committee transfer subject to (c). Same-Act phrase substitutions retained separately; no historical funding amounts silently treated as current and no whole-Act/PHS-program application.

DIVISION G--DEPARTMENTS <<NOTE: Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2015. Department of Labor Appropriations Act, 2015.>> OF LABOR, HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, AND EDUCATION, AND RELATED AGENCIES APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2015 

Sec. 506. (a) None of the funds appropriated in this Act, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are appropriated in this Act, shall be expended for any abortion. (b) None of the funds appropriated in this Act, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are appropriated in this Act, shall be expended for health benefits coverage that includes coverage of abortion. (c) The term ``health benefits coverage'' means the package of services covered by a managed care provider or organization pursuant to a contract or other arrangement. Sec. 507. (a) The limitations established in the preceding section shall not apply to an abortion-- (1) if the pregnancy is the result of an act of rape or incest; or (2) in the case where a woman suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness, including a life-endangering physical condition caused by or arising from the pregnancy itself, that would, as certified by a physician, place the woman in danger of death unless an abortion is performed. (b) Nothing in the preceding section shall be construed as prohibiting the expenditure by a State, locality, entity, or private person of State, local, or private funds (other than a State's or locality's contribution of Medicaid matching funds). (c) Nothing in the preceding section shall be construed as restricting the ability of any managed care provider from offering abortion coverage or the ability of a State or locality to contract separately with such a provider for such coverage with State funds (other than a State's or locality's contribution of Medicaid matching funds). (d)(1) None of the funds made available in this Act may be made available to a Federal agency or program, or to a State or local government, if such agency, program, or government subjects any institutional or individual health care entity to discrimination on the basis that the health care entity does not provide, pay for, provide coverage of, or refer for abortions. (2) In this subsection, the term ``health care entity'' includes an individual physician or other health care professional, a hospital, a provider-sponsored organization, a health maintenance organization, a health insurance plan, or any other kind of health care facility, organization, or plan.
